learningObjectives: Explain how Vision AI identifies and steers controls, and which technologies it uses.
Distinguish Vision AI from conventional property-based scanning and from image-based controls.
Describe User Identified Controls (UIDCs) and the role of anchors within Vision AI.
Judge when Vision AI is the appropriate scanning approach.

elements.text: ⚠️ This is the OPTIONAL section of the AE1 course. The Final Exam draws no questions from optional sections, so nothing here will be tested. It is worth understanding anyway — Vision AI is where Tosca's control identification is heading, and it directly addresses the weaknesses of the image-based controls covered in Lesson 8.

elements.term: Seeing the UI the way a person does
elements.description: Conventional scanning reads an application's technical structure — element ids, class names, the control tree. Vision AI instead analyses the application's visual components, using two neural networks: one for finding controls and one for optical character recognition (OCR). It identifies what is on screen much as a human tester would: this looks like a text field, that is a button labelled 'Submit'.

elements.term: Recognising control types, not just pixels
elements.description: The crucial detail is that Vision AI detects control types and adjusts its steering mechanism to the classification it has made. Having decided a region is a dropdown, it steers it as a dropdown. This is what separates it from raw appearance matching.

elements.title: Vision AI Modules in the AE1 workspace (Standard modules → TBox XEngines → Vision AI)
items: Run VisionScript — executes a VisionScript, Tosca's scripting layer for Vision AI driven steering.
Vision AI Self Healing — the self-healing counterpart for visually recognised controls.

elements.text: The presence of a dedicated 'Vision AI Self Healing' Module is worth noting against Lesson 5: conventional self-healing covers DotNet, Java, Oracle, UIA, XBrowser and Salesforce, and does not extend to image-based controls. Vision AI brings its own self-healing mechanism for visually identified controls — which is exactly the gap image-based identification leaves open.

bulletPoints: Two neural networks: control detection + OCR.
Identification is by visual components in the UI, not by technical attributes.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Vision AI vs the two methods you already know

elements.description: Property-based identification depends on technical attributes staying stable. Vision AI steers by visual components instead, which makes it resilient to UI changes that alter the underlying markup without changing what the user sees — a framework upgrade that renames every generated class, for example.

This is the comparison that matters most. Image-based identification matches a screenshot — it knows nothing about what the control is, only what it looked like. Vision AI recognises individual control types and adjusts its behaviour accordingly, which is smarter steering than pixel matching or screenshot comparison. Where Lesson 8's method is a last resort accepting brittleness, Vision AI aims to be a genuine identification strategy.

elements.text: Tricentis positions Vision AI as producing stable, self-healing Modules for any UI — the self-healing framing is deliberate, contrasting with image-based controls, which self-healing does not cover.

bulletPoints: Property-based: reads structure. Image-based: matches pixels. Vision AI: recognises control types visually.
Vision AI ≠ a better screenshot matcher — it classifies what it sees and steers accordingly.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: When automatic recognition is not enough

elements.description: Vision AI does not always classify a control correctly on its own. When standard recognition falls short, controls can be configured manually, or you can create User Identified Controls — controls you define yourself so the AI knows how to treat them.

UIDCs use anchor points — surrounding elements that guide the AI to locate the target correctly. The same relational idea you met in the PDF Engine lesson and in XScan's Advanced Identification appears here too: when an element is hard to pin down on its own, describe it by what sits around it.

elements.text: Three lessons, one recurring principle: PDF anchors, XScan anchor identification, and Vision AI anchor points all solve the same problem — identifying something unstable by reference to something stable nearby.

bulletPoints: UIDC = a control you define manually when the AI's own classification is insufficient.
Anchor points guide the AI to the right target.

elements.title: Vision AI fits when
items: Application controls lack reliable technical identifiers.
UI layouts change frequently but the visual appearance stays consistent.
You want self-healing behaviour for visually recognised controls.
Standard property-based identification has proved insufficient.

elements.text: Note what this list does not say: it is not positioned as a replacement for property-based scanning where that works well. Structural identification remains the default; Vision AI is the answer when structure is unavailable or unstable.
📄 The Vision AI Theory section is optional course material. Official Tricentis Academy content is not redistributed here — explore it inside the official course if you want the hands-on walkthrough.

bulletPoints: Best fit: no reliable identifiers, or markup that churns while the UI looks the same.

examPitfalls.title: Studying this section for the Final Exam
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Spending exam preparation time on Vision AI because it seems important.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Vision AI Theory is an optional section and the Final Exam draws no questions from optional sections. Learn it for its practical value, not for the exam.

examPitfalls.title: Equating Vision AI with image-based controls
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Assuming Vision AI is simply a more advanced screenshot matcher.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Image-based identification matches appearance with no understanding of the control. Vision AI recognises individual control types and adjusts its steering to that classification — a different mechanism, not a refinement of the same one.

examPitfalls.title: Replacing working property-based scans with Vision AI
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Migrating stable, well-identified Modules to Vision AI on the assumption that newer is better.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Vision AI targets cases where technical identifiers are unreliable or absent, or where markup changes while appearance does not. Where property-based identification already works, there is no problem for it to solve.

examPitfalls.title: Expecting perfect automatic classification
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Assuming Vision AI will correctly identify every control with no manual intervention.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: When standard recognition fails, controls can be configured manually or defined as User Identified Controls (UIDCs), using anchor points to guide the AI to the correct target.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which two technologies does Vision AI use to identify UI elements?

options.text: The DOM parser and the UI Automation framework.
Two neural networks — one for finding controls and one for optical character recognition (OCR).
The Appium server and the Mobile Agent.

practiceQuiz.hint: One network locates things; the other reads text.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Vision AI employs two neural networks: one for finding controls and one for OCR. Together they let it identify elements by their visual components rather than by technical attributes.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What is the essential difference between Vision AI and image-based controls?

options.text: There is none — both match screenshots.
Vision AI recognises individual control types and adjusts its steering accordingly, rather than performing simple pixel matching or screenshot comparison.
Image-based controls use neural networks; Vision AI does not.
Vision AI only works on mobile applications.

practiceQuiz.hint: One method understands what a control is; the other only knows what it looked like.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Image-based identification matches appearance with no knowledge of the control's nature. Vision AI detects control types and adapts its steering mechanism to the classification, which is why Tricentis describes it as producing stable, self-healing Modules.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Vision AI fails to classify a particular control correctly. What can you do?

options.text: Nothing — Vision AI classifications cannot be overridden.
Configure the control manually or create a User Identified Control (UIDC), using anchor points to guide the AI to the target.
Switch the whole Module to the Mobile Engine.
Retake the screenshot at a higher resolution.

practiceQuiz.hint: There is a named mechanism for controls you define yourself.
practiceQuiz.rationale: When standard recognition fails you can configure controls manually or create User Identified Controls (UIDCs). UIDCs use anchor points — surrounding elements that guide the AI to locate the target correctly.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which situation is the strongest case for using Vision AI?

options.text: A stable application whose controls all have reliable, unchanging ids.
An application whose markup changes frequently while its visual appearance stays consistent.
Reading values from an Excel workbook.

practiceQuiz.hint: Think about when structural identification stops being dependable.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Vision AI suits applications lacking reliable technical identifiers, or where UI layouts change frequently but the appearance remains consistent. Where identifiers are already stable, property-based identification has no problem for Vision AI to solve — and PDFs and Excel have their own dedicated engines.

quickRecap.value: OPTIONAL section — not covered by the Final Exam.
Two neural networks: control detection + OCR; identifies by visual components in the UI.
Resilient to markup changes that don't alter what the user sees.
Recognises control TYPES and adapts steering — not pixel matching or screenshot comparison.
User Identified Control — manually defined when automatic recognition falls short.
Surrounding elements that guide the AI to the target — the same relational principle as PDF and XScan anchors.
No reliable identifiers · frequent layout churn with stable appearance · property-based identification insufficient.
